name: Kaunertaler Gletscherstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaunertaler Gletscherstraße leads over 26 km and 29 hairpin turns up to 2,750 m: past the Gepatsch-Stausee reservoir directly to the foot of eternal ice.
preis: Maut PKW ca. 32,00 €, Motorrad ca. 24,00 € (mit Bergbahnticket/Skipass frei)
oeffnungszeiten: Ganzjährig geöffnet (im Winter mit Winterausrüstung befahrbar)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Kaunertaler Gletscherstraße is one of the most spectacular and highest toll-paying high-alpine roads in the entire Alps. Starting from the mountaineering village of Feichten in the Kaunertal at an altitude of 1,287 metres, the 26-kilometre panoramic road winds through 29 numbered hairpin bends up to 2,750 metres above sea level directly to the edge of the Weißseeferner glacier. The route overcomes nearly 1,500 metres of elevation gain and leads travellers through five alpine vegetation zones – from lush valley meadows and ancient stone pine forests to the rugged high-alpine primordial landscape of perpetual ice.

Construction History & Scenic Highlights

The road was built between 1979 and 1980 under the leadership of Kaunertal tourism pioneer Eugen Larcher to revitalise the Kaunertal economy and open the Weißseeferner to tourism. Masterfully integrated into the rugged rock landscape, the road passes numerous natural and engineering monuments: at around 1,765 metres lies the monumental Gepatsch-Stausee: the six-kilometre reservoir operated by TIWAG was constructed between 1961 and 1964; its 153-metre-high rockfill dam ranked among the highest in Europe at the time. Directly above the reservoir stands the historic Gepatschhaus (1,928 m) – Austria's oldest Alpine Club hut, built in 1873 by the Frankfurt am Main section of the DAV. Along the bends, 29 educational adventure stations provide information on geology, glacial moraines, alpine flora, and hydroelectric power generation. The road terminates right at the foot of the glacier at Restaurant Weißsee at 2,750 metres, allowing visitors to step directly onto the glacier ice without needing a cable car.

Visit & Getting There

The Kaunertaler Gletscherstraße is open year-round (in winter it is cleared and secured as the access route to the glacier ski resort; winter equipment required). Toll charges (2025/2026 season): passenger car day ticket approx. €32.00, motorcycle approx. €24.00; for skiers and visitors holding a valid cable car ticket, road use is free of charge (toll is included in the cable car ticket or ski pass). Arrival by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 or Arlbergschnellstraße S16 to Landeck/Prutz, then on the Kaunertalstraße L18 through Feichten to the toll station in the Platz district. By public transport: ÖBB to Landeck-Zams station, from where Postbus line 230 runs regularly via Feichten up to the Kaunertaler Gletscher.

Tips

The glacier road is completely asphalted, built with two lanes, and easily navigable for campervans and touring coaches. Reaching up to 2,750 m, it is one of Europe's most accessible high-alpine destinations – people with reduced mobility can park right at the glacier's edge. On the return journey, plan a stop at the Gepatsch-Kapelle chapel and the Schlosswand-Klamm gorge.
